official_baselines.verified: CSEW and police recorded crime have different strengths, limitations and coverage and must not be interchanged.

official_baselines.contract: Latest published crime bulletin before March 2026 release
official_baselines.verified: Bulletins distinguish survey incidents, prevalence, statistical significance and police-recorded measures.
Dataset pages retain scheduled revisions, corrections and superseded files.

official_baselines.contract: Police recorded crime and outcomes user guide
official_baselines.verified: Recorded offences, assigned outcomes, outcome type and offence type are separate fields.
Recording quality can vary over time and between forces because of rules, systems and quality assurance.

release.name: Crime in England and Wales: year ending March 2026

rows.rule: CSEW is a sample survey source and remains distinct from police recorded crime.
rows.evidence: ONS user guide describes complementary sources with different strengths and limitations.

rows.rule: Police recorded crime is an administrative recording system governed by counting rules.
rows.evidence: Home Office rules define national recording and counting standards for notifiable offences.

rows.rule: Crime outcomes describe outcomes assigned to recorded offences, not victimisation prevalence.
rows.evidence: Home Office outcomes publications separate outcome type and offence type.

rows.rule: Fraud reporting data retains its separate reporting-system provenance.
rows.evidence: ONS user guide lists Report Fraud as an additional source.

rows.rule: Survey ASB experience and police-recorded ASB incidents are separate measures.
rows.evidence: ONS bulletin reports the measures separately.

rows.rule: Police recorded crime can include businesses, society and children outside adult household survey scope.
rows.evidence: ONS release descriptions distinguish broader police-recorded scope.

rows.rule: Accreditation or official-statistics status is retained per source and product.
rows.evidence: ONS identifies product-specific statistical status.

rows.rule: ONS and Home Office publisher identities are stored separately.
rows.evidence: ONS publishes bulletins and datasets; Home Office publishes rules and outcomes.

rows.rule: Every extraction identifies its exact edition and period.
rows.evidence: ONS dataset pages retain edition histories.

rows.rule: Bulletin, appendix, PFA, open-data and outcomes artifacts are distinct contracts.
rows.evidence: Official releases publish them separately.

rows.rule: Incident counts are not prevalence percentages or rates.
rows.evidence: ONS bulletins distinguish incidents from prevalence.

rows.rule: Prevalence is the proportion experiencing crime and is not an incident count.
rows.evidence: CSEW products publish survey estimates.

rows.rule: Incidence rates retain their stated population and denominator.
rows.evidence: ONS user guide documents source-specific measures.

rows.rule: Recorded offence counts are not all victimisation.
rows.evidence: Home Office rules define recorded crime coverage.

rows.rule: Outcome counts are assigned outcomes and not offence severity.
rows.evidence: Home Office tables separate outcome and offence types.

rows.rule: Outcome-rate denominators and cohort definitions are retained.
rows.evidence: Home Office user guide distinguishes outcomes assigned and recorded outcomes.

rows.rule: Percentage change requires the correct baseline and period pairing.
rows.evidence: ONS compares like-for-like year-ending periods.

rows.rule: Percentage-point change is not percentage change.
rows.evidence: Survey prevalence comparisons require measure-consistent arithmetic.

rows.rule: Rates per 1,000 preserve denominator population and geography.
rows.evidence: Official products can use different rate bases.

rows.rule: Project safety score is not an ONS statistic or official severity score.
rows.evidence: Official sources do not define the project score.

rows.rule: CSEW estimates retain confidence intervals where supplied.
rows.evidence: ONS user guide explains confidence intervals.

rows.rule: A change is not treated as meaningful without source significance or equivalent evidence.
rows.evidence: ONS bulletins label statistically significant survey changes.

rows.rule: Survey estimates contain sampling error and are not exact counts.
rows.evidence: ONS describes CSEW as a representative sample.

rows.rule: Question wording, ordering, mode and response effects are retained.
rows.evidence: ONS notes questionnaire-order effects can affect estimates.

rows.rule: Suppressed or unreliable cells remain missing, never zero.
rows.evidence: Official tables apply quality and disclosure controls.

rows.rule: Rounded values are not reverse-engineered into false precision.
rows.evidence: Official bulletins publish rounded estimates.

rows.rule: Provisional or revisable values retain revision status.
rows.evidence: ONS separates scheduled revisions from corrections.

rows.rule: Police-recorded quality can vary over time and between forces.
rows.evidence: OSR reports force-level and system effects.

rows.rule: Method or system changes create tagged comparability breaks.
rows.evidence: ONS and Home Office guides document changes.

rows.rule: Missing coverage, unavailable periods and non-response are not zero activity.
rows.evidence: Coverage and activity are distinct concepts.

rows.rule: Year-ending periods match exactly before comparison.
rows.evidence: ONS releases state explicit periods.

rows.rule: Annual outcomes financial years are not mixed with calendar-quarter releases.
rows.evidence: Home Office annual outcomes cover financial years ending March.

rows.rule: Rolling-year totals overlap and are not independent monthly observations.
rows.evidence: Quarterly releases use rolling year-ending periods.

rows.rule: Police Force Area data remain PFA-level context.
rows.evidence: ONS publishes dedicated PFA tables.

rows.rule: Community Safety Partnership values remain CSP-level context.
rows.evidence: Home Office publishes CSP tables.

rows.rule: National estimates do not become local or parcel estimates.
rows.evidence: ONS bulletin covers England and Wales.

rows.rule: PFA or CSP statistics cannot substitute for LSOA observations.
rows.evidence: Official products distinguish geography levels.

rows.rule: No official release artifact supplies exact parcel crime measurements.
rows.evidence: Products are national, area, survey or approximate street-level.

rows.rule: CSEW age and household eligibility scope is retained.
rows.evidence: ONS states household and person scope.

rows.rule: England and Wales scope is not extended to other UK nations.
rows.evidence: Official products state jurisdiction.

rows.rule: Only the latest non-superseded edition is eligible.
rows.evidence: ONS pages list superseded files and update reasons.

rows.rule: Corrections capture affected tables and dates.
rows.evidence: ONS appendix history contains correction notices.

rows.rule: Downloads require raw-byte SHA-256, size and type.
rows.evidence: Artifact manifest requires byte-level provenance.

rows.rule: Workbook sheets and table ranges are inventoried before extraction.
rows.evidence: Spreadsheet structure precedes field mapping.

rows.rule: Internal labels match year ending March 2026.
rows.evidence: Historical ONS corrections show labels can be wrong without data changes.

rows.rule: Each measure is tagged CSEW, police recorded crime, Report Fraud or outcomes.
rows.evidence: ONS user guide treats them as different systems.

rows.rule: Outcome type, offence count or prevalence is not converted into severity.
rows.evidence: Official sources do not define a project severity transformation.

rows.rule: Aggregate evidence is not used for individual behaviour or risk inference.
rows.evidence: Products publish aggregate statistics.

rows.rule: Prepared semantics do not change stored values without live runtime acceptance.
rows.evidence: Canonical task requires live endpoint and browser acceptance.

rows.rule: Completion requires commit ancestry and remote readback.
rows.evidence: Canonical contract forbids PUBLISHED without readback.

quality_guards: CSEW, police recorded crime, Report Fraud and outcomes remain distinct.
Counts, prevalence, rates, changes and outcomes are not interchanged.
Uncertainty, significance, revisions and recording effects are retained.
National, PFA and CSP evidence is AREA_LEVEL_PROXY, not LSOA or parcel measurement.
No metric becomes a direct score input without runtime acceptance.
Completion requires ancestry and remote readback.
